answer: Permissionless identity without cost is a fable, so an agent economy can require epochal proof-of-space. Each agent seeds a large, incompressible graph from its public key and answers random-read Merkle challenges within tight latency limits. Because clones cannot share storage, scaling a tiny grove of agents into a vast orchard demands proportional physical disk space and IOPS per Sybil. However, cloud providers with cheap bulk drives still hold a steep cost advantage.
